A weaving track that flips the switch on slow fish.

As the spoon swims back to you, a weaving motion enters the track. That zigzag is what defines the NOA-S, and it is what flips the switch on fish in a slow mood.

The 1.4 g and 1.0 g are chosen mainly by retrieve speed, but each weight weaves differently, so it is worth fishing both to feel it.

When the NOA-S is dialled in, nothing else comes close.

Nothing gets there faster, built for casting range on big water.

For sheer speed of coverage, nothing outdoes the NOA BOSS. It excels at long casts on large venues and at tracing the bottom where there is depth.

In the high-activity window right after stocking, the casting range and appeal put you ahead of the anglers around you.

The 3.5 g in particular can go off in the most surprising way on a slow presentation. The potential here is hard to measure.

The origin of Rodio Craft's spoons, at home in any area.

The NOA is where Rodio Craft's spoons began. Whatever the venue, this is the one to tie on as a pilot lure to read what the fish are doing.

Its strong appeal gets noticed and draws a bite even when your depth is a little off.

Between retrieve style and custom rings and hooks, it covers the whole range from an aggressive bite to a dead one. A classic for good reason.

A high-weight spoon that gets going fast and covers every situation.

The QM comes onto plane quickly and also lifts quickly, so you can wind it up through the column or use its weight to wind it down. The body measures 32mm long and 11mm wide.

It casts a long way, which makes it ideal for working the surface out wide, and fish are slow to wise up to it. The occasional slide in its action is what draws the bite.

The 2.8g comes standard with a Honeycomb T Hook #4 and a #2 split ring.

A small silhouette with outsized appeal.

The NOA Jr. keeps a small silhouette while still appealing strongly. The four weights exist to cover a wide span of retrieve speeds.

The 1.2 g is the most all-round of them and serves as the benchmark weight on fisheries across Japan.

Straight tracing, lifting, dropping — the whole water column is yours to work as you see fit.
